statement: Fix the prepared data, ε, s, and one smooth profile from Lemma 6.2. For each sufficiently large fixed N there is a smooth function y on MN such that k∆gb B0(y) = divgb (H0(y)Eb), y −→ 0 at infinity. (6.22) It satisfies y ≥ y0, y ≤ PN , y = Oj(r2−n ) for every fixed j, (6.23) where constants in the last estimates may depend on N and on the fixed profile. Moreover B0(y) is harmonic sufficiently far out, and lim R→∞ ∫ SR ∂νb y dAgb = H0(0) k ω|Q|. (6.24)
